is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles funestus field mosquitoes from Malawi and the laboratory hybrid strain FANG/FUMOZ.

reports_target_markers.evidence: Reports genotyping of Cyp6p9a R (CYP6P9a_R) and Cyp6p9b R (CYP6P9b_R) markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The main text reports allele frequencies for the Malawi field population (CYP6P9a_R = 73%, CYP6P9b_R = 99%) but does not state the sample size N genotyped for the field population in the main text or figures. Detailed genotype counts for field samples reside in supplementary files (Figures S2, S3). All detailed genotype frequency figures and counts in the main text (Figures 2-5) are for the laboratory hybrid strain FANG/FUMOZ.

african_field_population.evidence: Field mosquitoes were collected in Chikwawa, Malawi in 2021 and tested as F1 progeny.

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting field collections, bioassays, experimental hut trials, RNAi, and genotyping.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Primary study reporting new field collections from Chikwawa, Malawi in 2021.

supplement.evidence: Genotype counts and sample sizes for field-collected mosquitoes are reported in supplementary materials (Figures S2, S3, and Tables S1-S8), which were not provided.

assessment.summary: This study investigates the impact of the pyrethroid-resistance P450 markers CYP6P9a_R and CYP6P9b_R in Anopheles funestus on susceptibility to chlorfenapyr and clothianidin. Field mosquitoes were collected in Chikwawa, Malawi in 2021. However, genotype counts with sample size N for field populations are only presented in supplementary files, while main text genotype-phenotype association figures rely on a laboratory hybrid strain (FANG/FUMOZ).
exclusion_reasons: Lacks extractable genotype data with sample size N for field populations in the main text (data resides in supplementary materials).
